page_hint: Ch 15, §3 Worked Example, 'Attention FLOP comparison' paragraph
quoted_clause: Attention is two matmuls per token per head — Q·$K^{T}$ then ·V — each a multiply-accumulate of L²·d, so in FLOPs (2 per MAC) the per-layer cost is ≈ 4 × L² × d_model
observed: The derivation is mis-stated. For a single query token, Q·Kᵀ is (1×d)·(d×L) = L·d MACs and (QKᵀ)·V is (1×L)·(L×d) = L·d MACs, i.e. 4·L·d FLOPs per token per head. L²·d is the cost for all L query positions in one head, not per token. The final formula 4·L²·d_model per layer is correct, but it does not follow from the sentence as written, and a reader following the printed derivation literally gets a factor of L wrong.
correction: Rewrite: 'Attention is two matmuls per head — Q·Kᵀ then ·V — each L²·d MACs for the whole sequence (equivalently 4·L·d FLOPs per token per head); with 2 FLOPs per MAC and n_heads heads, the per-layer cost is 4·L²·d_model.'
evidence: Per token per head: 2 matmuls × L·d MACs × 2 FLOPs/MAC = 4·L·d = 4 × 9,200 × 128 = 4.71×10⁶ FLOPs. Across L tokens and 64 heads: 4·L²·d_model = 4 × 9,200² × 8,192 = 2.773×10¹² per layer — matches the printed ≈2.8×10¹². quoted_clause: when many users share similar prompt prefixes, the KV cache can be partially shared, reducing memory traffic
observed: Prefix reuse eliminates redundant prefill computation and redundant KV allocation for the shared prefix. It does not reduce the KV bytes that must be read from HBM during decode for that prefix — decode reads the full K/V history of every sequence at every step regardless of whether the prefix was computed or reused. As written, the sentence can lead the reader to expect a decode-time bandwidth saving from prefix caching, which is the mechanism the chapter elsewhere (decision map, §6) correctly attributes to batching and quantization.
correction: Rewrite: 'when many users share similar prompt prefixes, the shared prefix's KV need not be recomputed or re-allocated, which removes prefill FLOPs and KV capacity; the KV bytes for that prefix are still read during decode, so the saving is in compute and capacity, not in decode-time traffic.'
evidence: Decode attention reads the sequence's entire K/V history per step; the prefix's K/V must be resident and read whether it was just computed or restored from a cache. The savings from prefix reuse are (a) prefill FLOPs for the shared prefix and (b) KV capacity for the shared prefix.
